LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASS: DEMONSTRATIVE DETERMINERS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you identify objects that are near or far?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those, in a variety of texts
2. use demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASS: DEMONSTRATIVE DETERMINERS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASS: DEMONSTRATIVE DETERMINERS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those, in a variety of texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those, in a variety of texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those, in a variety of texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those, in a variety of texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to use demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those, in a variety of texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners to a partner. (skill: use demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those correctly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those, in a variety of texts.
3. Practise this skill: use demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those correctly.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you identify objects that are near or far?
2. How do we show that objects being referred to are singular or more?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those, in a variety of texts.
5. Be able to: use demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
